newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-EBRD bullish on Russia, warns on standard.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-EBRD bullish on Russia, warns on standard.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development is bullish on Russia and its reform process but says investors should insist on high standards of business conduct within the country.

In an interview with Reuters, EBRD deputy vice president Guy de Selliers said the Russian banking sector was becoming more resilient with more quality banks. "Systemic risks are less present so we'll continue to work with the local banks and provide them with funding and equity to help strengthen the better banks."
But he said it was critical for investors to insist on high standards of business conduct within the country.
"There is no doubt there is still a problem about how business is conducted in Russia.
"There is not enough discipline and trust and that makes it difficult for investors and lenders to operate, which damages the growth prospect," he said.

With regard to the long queue of Russian borrowers wanting to tap the international bond market, he said he feared investors would do "name-lending" without demanding adequate exposure on the part of the borrowers. "That's not healthy," he said.
"I hope we are not going to see a new version of what happened in the 70s (debt crisis)," he said.
"I've heard of offers made to certain oblasts (regions) and for some of these there is no real data to build a credit case which is worrying."
"I think the Russian Federation is right to ensure that other Russian entities approach the international bond market in an organised and disciplined way, de Selliers said."
